12.0.s.en: (1) Rehoboam reigns and consults the elders and the young men

12.0.0.en: Shechem: a city in the tribe of Ephraim, 50 km north of Jerusalem, now called Nablus; it is one of the cities of refuge in which the Levites lived (Josh 20:7), and it is considered a middle place among the tribes of the children of Israel. Joshua had set up an altar, and near it are the mountains Gerizim and Ebal, on which the blessings and the curses were proclaimed (Josh 8:33-35). Rehoboam: he became king at the age of 41, the son of an Ammonite wife of Solomon (ch. 14:21), and perhaps the firstborn son of Solomon, and he was not wise despite his advanced age, and we understand from this that Solomon did not care for the upbringing of his children and did not charge them to keep God's commandments as David did.

12.0.1.en: The representatives of the tribes went to Shechem to enthrone Rehoboam the son of Solomon as king. And here we notice the pressure of the tribes on Rehoboam to reign in Shechem, which is in Ephraim, in order to take him away from Jerusalem, which is in Judah, where his father and grandfather reigned and where the army that supports him is. The tribes planned to demand their own demands of Rehoboam, so that if he refused it would be easy to depose him, far from his tribe and his army that is in Judah. And because Rehoboam was weak in character, he yielded to their opinion, and they made him king in Shechem.

12.1.0.en: The yoke: the crosspiece of wood that is placed on the necks of the two animals that pull farming implements, and "your father made our yoke grievous" means that he pressed us and wearied us greatly.

12.1.1.en: Jeroboam had a strong and rebellious personality, so Solomon tried to kill him, and therefore he fled to Egypt (ch. 11:

12.1.2.en: 40.) When he heard, while in Egypt, of Solomon's death, he felt reassured and tried to return, and what encouraged him to do so was that those among his people who loved him sent for him to return and support them in demanding of the new king Rehoboam a lightening of the taxes and the harsh orders upon them, so he actually returned and led them in demanding of Rehoboam that he lighten his bondage over them, and they made this a condition for their submission to and service of the new king. And the people in this demand forgot the merits of Solomon's rule and his wisdom and his good organization of the kingdom, so that he gave them peace and they lived securely without wars. And we notice also that they did not care about rejecting the worship of idols that had spread in the kingdom because of Solomon's laxity, for their aim was their material comfort and not attachment to God and the rejection of strange gods.

12.1.3.en: And we find that Solomon had earlier cared to fortify himself, so he married Pharaoh's daughter to ensure Egypt's support for him and did not place all his reliance on God, and now there comes the rebel Jeroboam, whom Egypt had sheltered, to divide the kingdom in the reign of his son Rehoboam. For God alone is able to protect man and establish kings in their kingdom.

12.1.4.en: Place your reliance on God above everything, then use all the means as instruments in God's hand to solve your problems, and if some of them fail or are delayed, do not be troubled, because God alone is able to support you and keep you from every evil.

12.2.0.en: Rehoboam asked the representatives of the tribes for time to think, so that he could consult with his counselors about the matter, and they would return to him after three days, that he might tell them his decision in the matter.

12.3.0.en: Rehoboam began by consulting the wise elders with experience, who had assisted his father Solomon throughout his life, asking them what answer he should give the people.

12.3.1.en: And we notice that Rehoboam did not resort to prayer first, as his grandfather David used to do, for God is the true King of the kingdom, but what he did is considered a kind of wisdom, since he was not hasty in answering the people and took care to consult wise counselors.

12.3.2.en: It is good that you consult others who have opinion and counsel regarding the works you undertake, but it befits you first and before everything to seek God's counsel.

12.4.0.en: The elders answered him that if he would pledge himself to the people to look after their interests and win them to him with gentle words, they would be subject to him all his life. By his showing submission to their demands and pledging concern for their comfort, he would make them attached to him and serve him faithfully. And these are the qualities of a wise king, and this is what the Lord Christ, the King of kings, did, for He served His people not only by teaching them and healing their diseases but by laying down His life for them, so the hearts of His children became attached to Him and they gave their lives even to martyrdom.

12.5.0.en: Rehoboam wanted also to listen to what his young friends said, among whom he had grown up and from whom he chose new counselors, and perhaps they shared with him his life of luxury and some amusement, or recklessness. It is understood from his consulting the young men that he was not at ease with the counsel of the elders, perhaps because of his unwillingness to reduce his financial resources from taxes and his lack of concern for the interests and problems of the people.

12.6.0.en: The little finger: the smallest finger of the hand.

12.6.1.en: The loins: the lower part of the back, that is, what a person sits on.

12.6.2.en: The counsel of the young men was entirely different from the counsel of the elders, for they advised the king to speak to the people with arrogance and harshness, to frighten them and ensure their submission, and to say to them that my little finger is thicker than my father's loins, and this was a well-known, common proverb at that time, meaning I am stronger and harsher than he. And if my father enslaved you and subjected you to forced labor in his works harshly by beating you with whips, then whoever neglects his work or tries to rebel, I will chastise him with scorpions, which not only hurt like whips but poison the human body and kill it, and some see that scorpions are a kind of whip with pieces of iron that tear the skin severely.

12.6.3.en: And here we see the causes that led to Rehoboam's deviation, which are:

12.6.4.en: 1- He was pampered, so he had no long-suffering, and could not contain his people and their demands.

12.6.5.en: 2- His mother was an Ammonite, so she did not teach him God's commandments and to take refuge in Him.

12.6.6.en: 3- It is not mentioned that his father cared for his upbringing, because of his preoccupation with his desires.

12.6.7.en: 4- He was proud, so he had no readiness to learn and to be a disciple at the hands of the elders and their counsel.

12.6.8.en: 5- He was not wise enough to distinguish good counsel from bad.

12.6.9.en: It is fitting for us to choose our counselors from tried elders of pure spiritual conduct, and to listen to them and act on their counsel, and not hand over our will to inexperienced bad friends.

12.7.0.en: The representatives of the people came, and Jeroboam with them, to Rehoboam, as the king had set for them on the third day, to listen to what he had decided regarding their request.

12.8.0.en: Rehoboam used harsh words in addressing the people, following the counsel of the young men and forsaking the counsel of the elders, and said: my father was harsh to you and I will add to this harshness; my father used whips to subdue you, but I will use scorpions for that.

12.9.0.en: Rehoboam rejected the demands of the people with arrogance and folly, so God's grace left him, and thus the word of God by the mouth of His Shilonite prophet about the tearing of the kingdom was fulfilled (ch. 11:29-39).

12.10.0.en: What portion have we in David?: the meaning is that we have no rights with the house of David, which is represented by the unjust Rehoboam and his father, the harsh Solomon, and therefore this is considered a declaration of secession.

12.10.1.en: To your tents, O Israel: a clear call for the ten tribes to split from the tribe of Judah by returning to their dwellings to look for a king for themselves, and none remained with Judah except the tribe of Benjamin (v. 21) and some individuals of the children of Israel adjoining them, such as the Simeonites.

12.10.2.en: Now see to thine own house, David: they address David as the most important figure who appeared on the throne of the children of Israel, and (see) how his kingdom was torn apart in the reign of his grandson Rehoboam.

12.10.3.en: When it became clear to the people that the king rejected their demands, they declared their rebellion against him and against the house of David and decided to withdraw from the assembly and to split from the tribe of Judah. Or Rehoboam the king, who is of the offspring of David the son of Jesse, and what is meant by tents is the dwellings of the ten tribes.

12.11.0.en: There remained to Rehoboam only the people living in the cities of the tribe of Judah and their neighbors from the nearby tribes, namely the tribe of Benjamin and some of the tribe of Simeon.

12.12.0.en: King Rehoboam remained in Shechem, the place where they had made him king, and paid no attention to the words of rebellion that the delegates of the tribes led by Jeroboam had spoken, but continued to carry on his administration of the kingdom as if nothing had happened in the meeting with the tribes, and sent Adoram, who was in charge of subjecting the people to forced labor in the works the kingdom needed, so the people rose up against him in all fury and stoned him until he died. Of course this was an unwise act on Rehoboam's part, to send Adoram at this time, but his pride and impulsiveness made him act this way, especially since forced labor is a thing unwanted by the people and heavy on them, and it would have been better for him to send delegates from himself to come to an understanding and try to reunite the kingdom. At last Rehoboam became aware of the seriousness of the situation and of the tribes' having actually split from him, so he mounted his chariot and fled from Shechem to Jerusalem, to take refuge there among his tribe of Judah, because he feared that the people would stone him as they had Adoram.

12.12.1.en: May you humble yourself before God when any trial meets you and seek Him with lowliness and faith, and He will guide you to the truth whatever your errors may be. For repentance with humility pours upon you God's mercies and forgiveness, and He rescues you and guides you and keeps you.

12.13.0.en: Israel: what is meant is the ten tribes.

12.13.1.en: This was the beginning of the separation of the ten tribes of Israel from the kingdom of Judah until the day of the writing of this book. From here we see that the division of the kingdom into two kingdoms took place for the following reasons:

12.13.2.en: 1- The failure to turn back from the worship of idols, which Solomon began, by repentance and cleaving to God, so the throne of David lost God's protection and blessing.

12.13.3.en: 2- Rehoboam's not submitting to the counsel of the experienced elders.

12.13.4.en: 3- Rehoboam's lack of feeling for the people's feelings, and even his threatening them, which provoked them greatly and called them to division.

12.13.5.en: 4- A discipline for the tribes of Judah and Benjamin for their preoccupation with the worship of idols that Solomon introduced instead of the worship of God in His Temple.

12.13.6.en: 5- A discipline for the ten tribes for their preoccupation with the worship of idols, so they were deprived of going up to Jerusalem, and Jeroboam seduced them to the worship of the golden calves and the forsaking of God.

12.14.0.en: Jeroboam was well known to the children of Israel from his past efforts in the service of King Solomon and carrying out his building works, and they also knew of Solomon's hatred of him when he learned of the prophecy of his taking rule over ten of the tribes of Israel, so they decided to make him king over them. And of the tribes none remained in submission to Rehoboam except the tribe of Judah and Benjamin with it, v. 21.) And here we record three warnings from God of the division of the kingdom:

12.14.2.en: 2- From Ahijah the prophet to Jeroboam (ch. 11:29-32).

12.14.3.en: 3- From Shemaiah to Rehoboam (vv. 22-24). And the people's choosing Jeroboam as king over the ten tribes goes back to the following:

12.14.4.en: 1- His distinction in leading the work in the days of Solomon.

12.14.5.en: 2- That he is from the tribe of Ephraim, which is the largest of the tribes in number and has its strength and standing among the tribes.

12.14.6.en: 3- Jeroboam was known to Shishak king of Egypt, and this gives a kind of reassurance of the support of strong Egypt for the new kingdom.

12.14.7.en: 4- The prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam of his reigning over the ten tribes, for this gives a sense of God's good pleasure and His blessing of Jeroboam, although it was only a prophecy and God is pleased only with good works. And God permitted this evil as a discipline for Judah and the tribes for their going away from God.

12.14.8.en: By this the splitting of the kingdom into two kingdoms was accomplished, which are:

12.14.9.en: 1- The kingdom of Judah, which is followed by the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and whose capital is Jerusalem, and it is called the southern kingdom, and in it is the Temple of God, and its kings reigned by inheritance, that is, all of them from the offspring of David, and their number is 19 kings, some of them righteous and the others wicked, and one wicked queen reigned with them, Athaliah the daughter of Ahab king of Israel, who was not of the offspring of David and was killed after a short time of her reign, that is, the total of those who reigned over Judah is twenty kings and queen. The kingdom of Judah began after the division in the year 931 BC and ended with the Babylonian captivity and the destruction of Jerusalem in the year 586 BC, so the age of the kingdom was 345 years.

12.14.10.en: 2- The kingdom of Israel, which includes the remaining ten tribes and is called the northern kingdom, and its capital was first Shechem, then Penuel, then Tirzah, and finally Samaria, which remained its capital until its end. Its kings were all wicked and in most cases were not by inheritance, and 19 kings reigned over it. It began in the year 931 BC and ended with the Assyrian captivity in the year 722 BC, so the age of the kingdom was 209 years.

12.14.11.en: The kings of Judah and the kings of Israel were in enmity and fought from the beginning of the two kingdoms until the time of Asa king of Judah and Omri king of Israel. Then in the second period they were allied and cooperating, and this is from the reign of Jehoshaphat king of Judah and Ahab king of Israel until Ahaziah the son of Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah and Joram kings of Israel; that is, the period of peace between them was short, and then came after it the third stage, in which the two kingdoms were estranged and wars were between them until the end of the kingdom of Israel.

12.14.12.en: It is noticed that the kingdom of Israel ended before the kingdom of Judah by about 136 years.

12.14.13.en: Note: the years in the Old Testament are all approximate.

12.15.s.en: (3) The Lord prevents Rehoboam from fighting the tribes

12.15.0.en: In an attempt to regain what he had foolishly lost, and thinking that he was able to confront the rebellion of the tribes, Rehoboam gathered an army of 180 thousand men from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin against Israel, to fight Israel (the ten tribes).

12.16.0.en: Shemaiah: a prophet contemporary with Rehoboam and a chronicler of his reign.

12.16.1.en: The Lord commanded Shemaiah the prophet to declare to Rehoboam and all the people of Judah and Benjamin that the splitting of the ten tribes was by God's permission, so they should not try to fight them, because this was a divine discipline so that they might all repent, and they obeyed God and each returned to his house. And here we see a virtue appearing in Rehoboam, which is obedience to God in the end. If only he had prayed and known what God's will was and obeyed Him from the beginning, but unfortunately he did not continue in obeying God and fought the tribes.

12.16.2.en: Be obedient to God's commandments that you read in the Holy Bible and hear in the Church, and so you will rescue yourself from the snares of the demons and walk uprightly and keep your peace in your heart always.

12.17.0.en: Mount Ephraim: what is meant is the lands of the tribe of Ephraim, which are full of mountains.

12.17.1.en: Penuel: a city east of the Jordan at a distance of four miles, in which God appeared to Jacob (Gen 32:30). Gideon had pulled down its tower and killed its inhabitants (Judg 8:8, 9, 17), and then Jeroboam, the first of the kings of Israel, rebuilt and fortified it.

12.17.2.en: After Jeroboam split off with the ten tribes, he became king over them and took Shechem, in which Rehoboam had been, as the capital of his kingdom, to declare to the tribes that he was the new king and not Rehoboam. And he took care to build up the city, that is, to fortify it and complete its buildings, so that it might be the capital of his kingdom. And afterward he took as the capital of his kingdom Penuel. Thus Jeroboam tried to make the seat of his kingdom in cities that had spiritual memories for the people, to gain their love and their loyalty to him. And this was a political act on his part and not love of God or of the holy places.

12.18.0.en: Jeroboam was a man far from God, for despite his hearing a clear prophecy from Ahijah the Shilonite that God would give him the ten tribes, and that was actually accomplished, anxiety was still within him, so he thought with a human mind, not relying on God, and said that if the people went to offer their sacrifices in the Temple at Jerusalem, as the Law prescribes on the various occasions and especially at the three feasts, namely the feast of Passover and the harvest and Tabernacles (Deut 16), longing would take hold of them for the days of the unity of the tribes, and they would decide to submit to Rehoboam king of Judah and get rid of him and kill him.

12.18.1.en: A person sometimes forgets that all the good things he enjoys are a divine gift, so he fears their loss and seeks to retain them by human tricks, whose vanity he soon discovers, and he knows then that the Lord is the Giver and that He alone is able to preserve His gift.

12.19.0.en: Jeroboam did not take refuge in God in solving this problem, which was his fear of the people's leaving him, and forgot God's promise to give him the ten tribes, which He had actually given him, so he thought in a human way and consulted his counselors, and made two calves of gold, to show the greatness of his gods, and to resemble the house of God covered with gold, and this sin the counselors shared with Rehoboam. And he said to the people, these are your gods which brought you up out of the land of Egypt, that is, these two calves are an image of Jehovah, and he put one of them in the north at Dan and the other in the south at Bethel so that it would be easy for all the inhabitants of the kingdom of Israel to reach them. And by Jeroboam's saying these are your gods that brought you out of the land of Egypt, and not saying your God, he led the people to fall into the worship of many idols. And the counselors' suggestion to Jeroboam that he set up two golden calves shows the extent of the spread of idol worship among the people and his counselors because of Solomon.

12.19.1.en: And the counselors deceived the people and told them that these calves are an image of Jehovah, and the people believed, and with time they became accustomed to the worship of idols, although the commandment (Ex 20:4) clearly forbade making images because they would lead the people astray from God. And by setting up the two calves Jeroboam committed many errors, which are:

12.19.2.en: 1- He did not trust in God, who had promised him kingship by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite.

12.19.3.en: 2- He kept the people away from the worship of God in His Temple.

12.19.4.en: 3- He introduced idol worship into the kingdom of Israel in the form of these two calves.

12.19.5.en: 4- This work of his helped in the entry of the gods of the pagan nations into the kingdom of Israel, since it gave them the idea of a plurality of gods.

12.19.6.en: 5- He did not learn from the error of the people in the days of Aaron when he made the golden calf and said to the people, "These be thy gods, O Israel" (Ex 32:4), so God was angry and killed thousands of the people by the hand of Moses.

12.20.0.en: This was a return to pagan worship, and the people used to go to Dan or Bethel, whichever was nearer to the place of their dwelling, so the matter was a great sin into which Jeroboam fell and into which he made his subject people fall.

12.21.0.en: Jeroboam continued in his evils, for he was not content with setting up the two calves but also set up altars on the high places, that is, the hills and plateaus, for the worship of God, contrary to the commandments of God, who commanded that worship be in His holy Temple only in Jerusalem. And when the Levites saw his immersion in evil, they left the cities of the kingdom of Israel and went to Jerusalem, so as not to anger God by taking part in these evil forms of worship (2 Chr 11:13, 14). Then Jeroboam continued in his evil, and set up priests and ministers for these strange forms of worship from the other tribes besides the tribe of Levi. And his saying "of the lowest of the people" means from the various classes, even the lowly among them, in an attempt to draw the hearts of the people toward him, by having priests be from all classes, and in all this he neglected God and rejected His commandments.

12.22.0.en: Persisting in his evil, Jeroboam made a feast for his gods that he had made in Bethel and Dan.

12.22.1.en: And he set this feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, as a substitute for the feast of Tabernacles, which God commanded after the feast of the harvest and which is on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. He put it a month after the feast of Tabernacles because the harvest is later in the northern kingdom than in the southern, but the real motive behind holding this feast at this time was to keep the people away from the feasts that God commanded. And here Jeroboam sinned by instituting a feast from his own ideas and not from God, for the worship of his idols. He concentrated the worship in Bethel, because Jeroboam himself used to pray in this place, as the Book of Amos tells us (Amos 7:13), and Jeroboam offered sacrifices in Bethel, perhaps offering them himself, and this is a usurpation of the priesthood, and all this had the outward form of the worship of God but was in truth the worship of idols, and by this Jeroboam led his people astray after the worship of idols and made all the kings who came after him fall into the same errors.

12.22.2.en: And we notice that God did not strike him with leprosy like King Uzziah (2 Kgs 15:5), because Jeroboam did not go up to burn incense on God's holy altar, as Uzziah did, but went up to an altar of idols, which needs no priesthood. And we notice that he makes light of God and deceives by pretending to be a good king who does not want to burden his people with travelling to Jerusalem, whereas the truth is that he wants to keep his people away from Rehoboam lest they submit to him.

12.22.3.en: And perhaps among the things that encouraged Jeroboam to worship idols was what Solomon, the king before him, did in spreading pagan forms of worship among the children of Israel.

12.22.4.en: If you fall into an error, examine yourself and repent, so that you do not persist in it and the error drags you into many other errors. Humble yourself and seek God, and He will rescue you and bring you back to Him.

12.22.5.en: Prophecy of the destruction of the pagan altars (1) Prophecy about Josiah (vv. 1-10)

12.22.6.en: 1- And, behold, there came a man of God out of Judah by the word of the LORD unto Bethel: and Jeroboam stood by the altar to burn incense. 2- And he cried against the altar in the word of the LORD, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith the LORD; Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men's bones shall be burnt upon thee. 3- And he gave a sign the same day, saying, This is the sign which the LORD hath spoken; Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out. 4- And it came to pass, when king Jeroboam heard the saying of the man of God, which had cried against the altar in Bethel, that he put forth his hand from the altar, saying, Lay hold on him. And his hand, which he put forth against him, dried up, so that he could not pull it in again to him. 5- The altar also was rent, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the LORD. 6- And the king answered and said unto the man of God, Intreat now the face of the LORD thy God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored me again. And the man of God besought the LORD, and the king's hand was restored him again, and became as it was before. 7- And the king said unto the man of God, Come home with me, and refresh thyself, and I will give thee a reward. 8- And the man of God said unto the king, If thou wilt give me half thine house, I will not go in with thee, neither will I eat bread nor drink water in this place: 9- For so was it charged me by the word of the LORD, saying, Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor turn again by the same way that thou camest. 10- So he went another way, and returned not by the way that he came to Bethel.
